# Gram-positive rods

> *Why can some of these bacteria survive boiling, and why does one toxin explain a whole disease?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
This chapter will follow the layout of [*Gram-positive cocci*](gram-positive-cocci.qmd). The plan:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| The group in one sentence | Thick-walled rods; some survive as spores in soil and food, and several cause harm mainly through a single toxin |
| Sorting key | Spores or not; oxygen (Bacillus with oxygen, Clostridium without); growth inside cells |
| Main organisms | *Clostridium* (tetanus and botulinum toxins as single-toxin diseases), *Listeria* (cold growth, life inside cells) |
| Supporting organisms | *Bacillus cereus*, *Bacillus anthracis*, *Clostridioides difficile*, *Corynebacterium diphtheriae* |
| Later in the course | Tetanus, botulism, diphtheria and *C. difficile* in the infection, neurology and gut blocks; toxoid vaccines in immunology |
